episodes.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
episodes.headline: When context becomes lasting memory
episodes.description: Can useful context survive after the prompt disappears? A careful look at learning new behavior while preserving the old.
episodes.takeaway: Retest older examples after every update, even when the original weights stay frozen.
episodes.caveat: Fifty compatible factual edits are not indefinite lifelong learning. Replay also changes the optimization budget.

episodes.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
episodes.headline: A smaller cache. What survives?
episodes.description: Compress a document’s attention cache for questions that have not been asked yet.
episodes.takeaway: Preserve both what a memory returns and how strongly it competes for attention.
episodes.caveat: 16× describes logical key-value compression, not measured physical memory savings or faster inference. Preparation is expensive.

episodes.title: Enhancing Latent World Models with Associative Memory
episodes.headline: Better plans through associative memory
episodes.description: A compact memory bank helps a world model predict latent states and plan from images.
episodes.takeaway: Compact latent conditioning can help planning, but a learned prior is not a growing episodic memory.
episodes.caveat: Small simulation study; no inference-time write rule. The paper does not clearly define its error bars.

episodes.title: TimeCap: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Captioning Wearable Health Time-Series Data
episodes.headline: Auditable captions for wearable signals
episodes.description: Auditable rule-based captions for wearable time series, with preliminary prediction gains and clinical limitations.
episodes.takeaway: Use deterministic signal-language rules when reproducible annotations matter.
episodes.caveat: Self-reported outcomes, only fifteen positive atrial-fibrillation test participants and no external clinical validation; caption access is restricted.

episodes.title: PPG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for PPG Foundation Models
episodes.headline: Make a foundation model earn its complexity
episodes.description: A controlled benchmark asks when pulse-signal foundation models beat simple physiological and general-purpose controls.
episodes.takeaway: Compare pulse-signal models with constant, physiological-feature and general time-series controls using participant-level evaluation.
episodes.caveat: Retrospective benchmark results do not establish clinical utility. Confidence-interval overlap is not equivalence, and released recipes may not be optimally tuned.

episodes.title: Detecting Agitation Before Behavioral Escalation in Autistic Youth Through Multimodal Wearable Sensing
episodes.headline: Temporal evaluation changes the result
episodes.description: A small personalized sensing study reveals how temporal evaluation changes apparent agitation-detection performance.
episodes.takeaway: Audit personalization, labels, sensor contributions and chronological splits before treating a sensing model as an early-warning system.
episodes.caveat: Fifteen participants in clinician-led sessions; no unseen-child validation or demonstrated prevention of escalation. Earlier windows were not independently labeled as agitation.

episodes.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
episodes.headline: Reconstruct first, generate in one step
episodes.description: Reconstruction pretraining improves the quality-compute frontier of one-step image generation.
episodes.takeaway: An easy reconstruction objective can prepare a generator for harder distribution matching; compare the complete quality-compute frontier.
episodes.caveat: Compute multipliers depend on the baseline. Video prediction resets from real observations and does not establish stable simulation or improved control.

episodes.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
episodes.headline: Continuous thought, explicit tool calls
episodes.description: Continuous internal reasoning combines with explicit text tool calls and persistent mixed attention state.
episodes.takeaway: Combine latent recurrence with text actions and persistent mixed state, then measure complete latency, memory and correctness.
episodes.caveat: The attention cache grows. Estimated decoding cost excludes prompt processing and external tools; readable latent readouts are not proof of faithful explanations.

episodes.headline: A growing vector store, sixteen memory tokens
episodes.description: A learned reader compresses document embeddings into continuous inputs for a frozen language model.

episodes.title: RL-Guided Temporal Localization for Dual-Channel Retrieval in Long-Horizon Agent Memory
episodes.headline: TIDER uses date windows to recover memories semantic search misses
episodes.description: A trained temporal locator adds date-based candidates before answer generation. With the same memory pool and top-20 unit budget, LifeBench accuracy rises from 52.21% to 61.52%; transfer to LoCoMo exposes temporal-localization failures.

episodes.title: BeJEPA: A Goal-Conditioned Humanoid Behavior World Model via Unsupervised RL

episodes.description: A humanoid policy learns from a next-state predictor and a discounted summary of behavioral continuation. Balanced model-predictive refinement improves global tracking in the paper's simulation protocol, while local posture and hardware evidence remain qualified.

episodes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
episodes.headline: Must-read: trained read/write memory changes per-conversation state without retraining the backbone
episodes.description: Must-read: trained read/write memory changes per-conversation state without retraining the backbone; compare compression against recall fidelity.
episodes.takeaway: Token-level updates and response training matter more than branding.
episodes.caveat: The most useful ablation replaces token-level writes with one turn-level update: Nano’s average falls from forty-seven to forty-one. Removing response post-training falls further, to thirty-six point three. Changing the exact gated update formula has a much smaller effect. The reusable idea is therefore a learned write-and-read interface, not just a named update rule. For continual agents, test latent state alongside exact retrieval at matched evidence budgets. Measure forgotten details, not only bytes. Fixed state remains lossy, and autonomous experience acquisition and consolidation remain open problems.

episodes.headline: Continual robot RL separates new-task reward learning from old-task action matching, with important growing-memory and cost caveats.
episodes.description: Continual robot RL separates new-task reward learning from old-task action matching, with important growing-memory and cost caveats.
episodes.takeaway: Separate the roles of value transfer and behavioral memory.
episodes.caveat: The hardware stopping rule is nineteen successes in a rolling window of twenty episodes. There is no full hardware baseline sweep, and related assemblies may transfer more readily than unrelated tasks. Resetting the critic modestly worsens performance; updating it on old replay also hurts retention. However, the visual-encoder ablation changes both encoder identity and stability, so it cannot isolate representation drift. The key reusable design is to separate current reward learning from prior behavior preservation. Code is marked coming soon. Official footage is linked, not reproduced here.
